name: Customer volume confirmation
definition: Confirming monthly and daily delivered volumes with end-use and utility customers, and agreeing the volumes used for billing.

synthesis.description: Schedulers keep running month-to-date flow spreadsheets for utility and industrial customers such as HL&P, CP&L, Equistar and Mobil, and send updated numbers to the desk as the month goes on. Customers and pipelines send their own actuals or swing volumes back. Differences between Enron's system flow and the customer's meter, short days, plant outages and unrecorded deals are raised by email and resolved before the volumes are agreed for billing.
steps: Pull the latest daily flow for the customer meters from Enron's system or SCADA.
Update the customer's month-to-date spreadsheet and send it to the desk.
Receive the customer's or pipeline's actuals, swing volumes or best-available figures.
Compare the customer's figures with Enron's system flow and flag short days or differences.
Check whether a deal exists for any unexplained gas and whether it was billed.
Adjust nominations or volumes for outages and plant restarts the customer reports.
Agree the final monthly volumes and pass them on for billing.
synthesis.approach: A daily report that pulls metered flow from the scheduling system for each customer, lays it beside the customer's or pipeline's actuals in a fixed spreadsheet layout, and highlights days where the two differ or where no matching deal exists, so the scheduler only works the flagged days.
synthesis.rationale: Most rounds are the same month-to-date spreadsheet rebuilt and resent, and the trouble arises when system flow, customer meters and deals disagree. A standard reconciliation layout with system flow, customer flow, difference and deal columns would make every round consistent and surface mismatches early.
